name: The evening the edit takes
promise: Where an evening of editing actually goes, why searching by ear is the slow part, and what one pass removes.
note: First post written to the hook + slide-plan rules. Hook move: loss. Trigger word: stealing (Helper). Pays its promise on slide 2.

slides.title: Your edit is *stealing* an evening a week

art.s: a wall clock with its hands blurred into a single continuous ring, standing alone on a bare studio floor
art.c: the clock sits centre-right in the middle band of the frame; the entire lower-left third is bare empty floor, one flat unbroken colour with no objects and no pattern

items.title: Cut the filler
items.meta: Every um and uh, one at a time

items.title: Trim dead air
items.meta: Hundreds of gaps, none worth keeping

items.title: Clean the room
items.meta: Hum you stopped hearing an hour ago

items.title: Bleep one word
items.meta: Find it, cut it, time the tone

items.title: Mark the chapters
items.meta: Re-listen to find where it turns

items.title: Level the file
items.meta: Then listen to the whole thing again

slides.kicker: Notice what they have in common
slides.title: Every one of them is a *search*

slides.kicker: And searching is the slow part
a: Is a picture of loudness, not words
So you find a sentence by listening for it
Every search plays back in real time
b: So you find the sentence by reading it
Every search runs at the speed *you read*

slides.title: Read it, select it, *delete* it
items: Upload the recording and read the transcript that comes back
Select the tangent the way you would in any document
Delete — the audio under those words goes with them, crossfade included

art.s: a single clean ribbon of tape lifting free from a dense tangle, the tangle confined to the very top edge of the frame
art.c: the tangle is a narrow band across the TOP of the frame and nothing else; the whole lower two thirds is bare empty studio floor, one unbroken colour, no debris

art.s: an empty studio backdrop with one soft sweep of light across it and no objects at all
art.c: the entire frame is a plain unbroken sweep of colour with nothing in it — this slide carries eight tiles of type and the picture must stay out of their way

slides.title: Automatic cuts will *butcher* it
slides.note: Every cut is a line of text you can read before it happens — and put back after.

slides.kicker: So you know where it stops
slides.title: What it does *not* do
items: No video editing — this is audio only
No publishing: you still upload to your own host
Not a DAW, so no multitrack mixing or mastering
Music you bring yourself keeps its own licence

art.s: a desk lamp switched off, the room behind it empty and settled
art.c: the lamp sits low and to the right, small in frame; the whole centre and upper half is bare empty backdrop so centred type sits on nothing
